Slice: Change Email

Intent

Let a neighbor change the email address the shed uses for them, from My Account, so a wrong or outdated address can be put right and overdue and pickup emails reach them. The new address takes effect at once, and the old one is free for anyone to use.

Trigger & Actor

A neighbor, from their own My Account screen, for their own account. My Account offers Change Email on any account that isn't closed (INV-MYAC-9); a suspended neighbor is offered it and refused with a reason they can see. The shed manager doesn't change neighbors' emails.

Command / Input

Command: Change Email

A NeighborId is a UUID. Text has leading and trailing whitespace (any Unicode whitespace) removed; text that is empty after that counts as absent.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The account whose email changes, which must be the neighbor making the request (INV-CEM-1) and a registered account (INV-CEM-10).
email Text yes The new email. Trimmed; must not then be empty (INV-CEM-11), at most 254 characters, and shaped like an email address (INV-CEM-12). Must not be held by another account under INV-CEM-2, compared ignoring case. Kept as typed.

There is no name field: only the email can be changed. A neighbor's name stays as they registered it.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Account @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Email Changed → context Neighbors Read by: My Account and Neighbors (the email shown); Overdue Loans To Notify and Pickup Notices To Send (the address the next email goes to); Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors (the email shown to the shed manager).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command.
email Text yes From the command, trimmed. The account's current email from now on.
changedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

The event never changes. A later change records a new Neighbor Email Changed. An account's current email is the email of its latest Neighbor Email Changed, or of its Neighbor Registered if it has never changed it.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Email Changed updates the email in My Account, Neighbors, Overdue Loans To Notify, Pickup Notices To Send, Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors, each specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent: the new email shows once each has caught up. Every overdue or pickup email the shed sends from then on, including one for a loan or set-aside already waiting to be emailed, goes to the new address.

Invariants / Business Rules

Changing the email resends nothing. A notice already sent, or already recorded as undelivered, is not tried again at the new address: no further attempt is made after a failure (Record Overdue Notice Failure, INV-ONF-6).

  • INV-CEM-1: A neighbor changes their own email themselves, from My Account.
    • The request must come from the neighbor whose account it names. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch. The shed manager doesn't change neighbors' emails.
  • INV-CEM-2: The new email is refused if it belongs to an account that is not closed, or to a closed account that was suspended when it was closed.
    • This is the same one-account-per-email rule as at sign-up (INV-REG-4, Register Neighbor). An account's email is always its current one.
    • Emails are compared ignoring case. The account's own current email never counts as held by another account.
    • Whether a closed account was suspended when it was closed is read from its Neighbor Account Closed (whileSuspended), never worked out from earlier suspensions and reinstatements.
  • INV-CEM-3: A neighbor whose account is closed can't change their email.
    • After closing, My Account is read-only.
  • INV-CEM-3a: A suspended neighbor can't change their email. The change is refused with a reason they can see, and they can change it once reinstated.
    • Otherwise a suspended neighbor could change to a new address, close their account, and sign up again with their original address.
  • INV-CEM-4: Once changed, the account's email is the new one.
    • Every later check of INV-CEM-2 and INV-REG-4 treats the new email as held by this account.
  • INV-CEM-5: The old email is released.
    • No account holds it any more, so it can be used to sign up or by another neighbor's change.
  • INV-CEM-7: The new email takes effect at once, with no verification.
    • Neighbor Email Changed is recorded straight from the request; nothing is sent to the new address first.
  • INV-CEM-9: Asking to change the email to the one the account already has succeeds and records nothing.
    • The comparison is made after trimming, exactly as typed. So a repeated request, after a lost response, never records a second change. A request that differs from the current email only in capital letters is a change, and is recorded: it is how a neighbor corrects the capitalisation of their address.
    • The command carries no "from" email. A late copy of an older request, arriving after a later change, counts as a new request and changes the email again.
  • INV-CEM-10: The neighbor must be a registered account.
  • INV-CEM-11: A new email is required.
    • An email that is empty, or only whitespace, is missing.
  • INV-CEM-12: A new email is at most 254 user-visible characters, counted after trimming, and must be shaped like an email address: an "@" with at least one character before it and at least one after it.
    • A longer one is refused, never cut short. These are the same limits as at sign-up (INV-REG-10, INV-REG-11, Register Neighbor).
  • INV-CEM-13: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-CEM-1, INV-CEM-4, INV-CEM-7)
    • Given: Ana's account N1 is active with ana@oldmail.example, and no other account uses ana@example.org
    • When: Ana changes her email to ana@example.org from My Account
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, with ana@example.org and the time it was recorded. Nothing is sent to the new address first.
  • Whitespace is removed (INV-CEM-11)
    • Given: N1 is active with ana@oldmail.example
    • When: Ana changes her email to " ana@example.org "
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded with ana@example.org.
  • Same email as now (INV-CEM-9)
    • Given: N1's current email is ana@example.org
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to ana@example.org
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing is recorded.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-CEM-9)
    • Given: Neighbor Email Changed was recorded for N1, to ana@example.org
    • When: the same Change Email request for N1, ana@example.org, arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • No email (INV-CEM-11)
    • Given: N1 is active
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to an empty value, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with email-missing: "Please enter your email address." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by an active account (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Ben's active account N2 uses ben@example.org
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by a suspended account (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Cleo's account N3 uses cleo@example.org and is suspended
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to cleo@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used." No event is recorded.
  • Email of an account closed while suspended (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Dan's account N4, using dan@example.org, was closed while suspended
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to dan@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used." No event is recorded.
  • Email of an account closed while active (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Eve's account N5, using eve@example.org, was closed while active
    • When: Ana changes her email to eve@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, with eve@example.org.
  • Email held in different capitals (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Ben's active account N2 uses ben@example.org
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to Ben@Example.ORG
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used." No event is recorded.
  • Correcting capital letters (INV-CEM-2, INV-CEM-9)
    • Given: N1's current email is ana@example.org
    • When: Ana changes her email to Ana@Example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, with Ana@Example.org. Her own account doesn't count as holding the address.
  • Email not shaped like an address (INV-CEM-12)
    • Given: N1 is active
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to ana.example.org
    • Then: refused with email-invalid: "Please enter a valid email address." No event is recorded.
  • Email too long (INV-CEM-12)
    • Given: N1 is active
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to an address of 255 characters
    • Then: refused with email-too-long: "Your email address can be at most 254 characters." No event is recorded.
  • Old email released (INV-CEM-5)
    • Given: Ana changed N1's email from ana@oldmail.example to ana@example.org
    • When: Ben asks to change N2's email to ana@oldmail.example
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N2, with ana@oldmail.example.
  • The new email is held from then on (INV-CEM-4)
    • Given: Ana changed N1's email to ana@example.org
    • When: Ben asks to change N2's email to ana@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-CEM-3a)
    • Given: N1 is suspended, with ana@oldmail.example
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to ana@example.org
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't change your email while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Changing the email after reinstatement (INV-CEM-3a)
    • Given: N1 was suspended and has since been reinstated, and no other account uses ana.ruiz@example.org
    • When: Ana changes her email to ana.ruiz@example.org from My Account
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, with ana.ruiz@example.org.
  • Closed account (INV-CEM-3)
    • Given: N1 is closed, with ana@oldmail.example
    • When: a change of N1's email to ana@example.org is requested
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • A request for someone else's account (INV-CEM-1)
    • Given: N1 and N2 are both active
    • When: a request from Ben asks to change N1's email
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only change your own email." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-CEM-10)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: a change of N9's email is requested
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-CEM-13)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for changing an email arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on My Account. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-CEM-13): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-CEM-1): who is asking is settled next, before any other rule.
  3. neighbor-not-found (INV-CEM-10).
  4. email-missing, then email-too-long, then email-invalid (INV-CEM-11, INV-CEM-12).
  5. The new email is the account's current one (INV-CEM-9): succeeds with nothing recorded.
  6. account-closed (INV-CEM-3).
  7. neighbor-suspended (INV-CEM-3a).
  8. email-in-use (INV-CEM-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-CEM-13
requester-mismatch You can only change your own email. INV-CEM-1
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-CEM-10
email-missing Please enter your email address. INV-CEM-11
account-closed This account is closed. INV-CEM-3
neighbor-suspended You can't change your email while your account is suspended. INV-CEM-3a
email-too-long Your email address can be at most 254 characters. INV-CEM-12
email-invalid Please enter a valid email address. INV-CEM-12
email-in-use That email address can't be used. INV-CEM-2

neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. email-missing, email-too-long, email-invalid, email-in-use, account-closed and neighbor-not-found mean the same conditions as in Register Neighbor and Check Out Tool. email-in-use is one reason for every case of INV-CEM-2, worded to be true in each, so a refusal never reveals another account's status; its sentence fits a change rather than a sign-up.

Idempotency: there is no request ID. A request whose effect has already happened, because the account's current email is already the one asked for, succeeds and records nothing (INV-CEM-9).

Requests at the same moment: the email check and the recording of Neighbor Email Changed happen as one step, shared with Register Neighbor, so no two accounts are ever given the same email. Of two requests for the same email at once, from a sign-up or a change, at most one is recorded; the other is refused with email-in-use.

There are no retries, compensations or external calls in this slice. Nothing is emailed when the email changes.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may change only their own email (INV-CEM-1); the shed manager doesn't change neighbors' emails. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Email Changed holds the neighbor's new email address. The old address stays in the earlier events as the shed's record. Names and emails are kept with the shed's history and never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time email check above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (this slice): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId. Used for INV-CEM-3a (this neighbor's own suspension).
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId. Used for INV-CEM-3a.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId, whileSuspended.
    • These match slices/register-neighbor.md, slices/suspend-neighbor.md and slices/reinstate-neighbor.md. Close Account is specified in a slice being written in depth; it is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Account, Neighbors, Overdue Loans To Notify, Pickup Notices To Send, Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors (the email). Register Neighbor and later Change Email requests check the new email as held.

Open Questions

None.

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v1: v1 keeps the old view names in prose; the views named no longer exist in the model; deferred to v2 (2026-11-01, Mike Key)
"},{"index":1,"name":"Check Out Tool","x0":289.76,"x1":433.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Check Out Tool

Intent

Let a neighbor borrow a tool, self-service, from the Tool Catalog. The checkout opens a loan with a due date set from the tool's default checkout period, or from a shorter period the neighbor chooses. It is also how a holder collects a tool set aside for them: there is no separate pickup.

Trigger & Actor

The neighbor who will borrow the tool, from the Tool Catalog screen, on a tool the catalog offers Check Out on (available, reserved or set aside). The shed manager does not record checkouts. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID.

Command / Input

Command: Check Out Tool

A LoanId, ToolId or NeighborId is a UUID. One clock reading is taken when the command is handled. "Today" is that moment's calendar date in the shed's local time zone, and the event's checkedOutAt is that same moment.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
loanId LoanId yes A UUID chosen by the caller for the new loan, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different loan already recorded (INV-CHK-12).
toolId ToolId yes The tool to borrow. Must be a tool that has been added (INV-CHK-11).
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor borrowing it, who must be the one making the request (INV-CHK-1). Must be a registered account (INV-CHK-11).
loanPeriodDays Int no Optional. Whole days, from 1 up to the tool's default checkout period (INV-CHK-6). When absent, the default applies. A fractional value is refused, never rounded.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Catalog @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Checked Out → context Loans Read by: Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog and My Loans; My Holds, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire and Pickup Notices To Send (a holder's checkout ends their hold); Overdue Loans To Notify and Neighbors To Flag (the loan's due date); Undelivered Notices (loan details shown there).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command. Identifies the loan everywhere from here on.
toolId ToolId yes From the command.
toolName Text yes Set by the system: the tool's name as recorded by Tool Added, copied so the loan's readers never look it up.
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command: the borrower.
neighborName Text yes Set by the system: the borrower's name as recorded by Neighbor Registered.
neighborEmail Text yes Set by the system: the borrower's email current at checkout (Neighbor Registered, replaced by any Neighbor Email Changed). Readers that email later keep the address current themselves.
loanPeriodDays Int yes The period the loan started with: loanPeriodDays from the command, or the tool's default checkout period when it was absent.
dueDate Date yes Set by the system: the checkout date (today) plus loanPeriodDays. A later Loan Extended sets a new dueDate; this one never changes.
checkedOutAt Instant yes Set by the system: the UTC moment of the clock reading above. Its date in the shed's local time zone is the checkout date.

The event doesn't name the hold it ends. A holder has at most one hold on a tool, so readers match the ended hold by toolId and neighborId (INV-CHK-9).

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Checked Out changes the tool's entry in Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog, starts the loan's entry in My Loans, and ends the borrower's hold on the tool in My Holds and the hold to-do lists. Each view is specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-CHK-1: A neighbor checks a tool out themselves, for themselves.
    • The command names the acting neighbor in neighborId, and the request must come from that neighbor (requester-mismatch otherwise). The shed manager does not record checkouts. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account.
    • A caller with no sign-in is refused with not-signed-in, before anything else is checked.
  • INV-CHK-2: A tool that is already checked out can't be checked out again until it is returned or recorded lost.
    • A loan is open from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan.
  • INV-CHK-3: A tool set aside for a holder can be checked out only by that holder, until the end of the collect-by date.
    • A tool is set aside from Hold Fulfilled for a hold until that hold ends. The collect-by date is Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate, recorded on the event; this slice reads it and never works it out.
    • The holder's pickup is an ordinary checkout. There is no separate pickup event.
  • INV-CHK-3a: A tool that is back in the shed with holds waiting, and not set aside, can be checked out only by the neighbor whose hold is at the front of the queue.
    • This holds after a return before Hold Fulfilled is recorded, and after a set-aside ends before the next hold is fulfilled.
    • The front of the queue is the hold on the tool, still waiting, whose Hold Placed was recorded first. Queue order is the order the Hold Placed events were recorded, never a comparison of times.
  • INV-CHK-3b: A holder's claim on a set-aside tool ends at the start of the day after the collect-by date, shed local time, whether or not Hold Expired has been recorded yet.
    • From that moment the set-aside is treated as ended. If a hold is waiting, only the neighbor at the front of the queue can check the tool out (INV-CHK-3a), and the former holder is refused. If none is waiting, anyone can, the former holder included.
  • INV-CHK-4: A retired tool can't be checked out.
    • A tool recorded lost is retired by that, so it can't be checked out either.
  • INV-CHK-5: A neighbor with an overdue loan can't check out a tool.
    • A loan is overdue from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time, while it is still open. The due date is the latest one set by Tool Checked Out or Loan Extended. Nothing records it; it is worked out from the due date and today.
    • Any open loan counts, including one whose tool has since been retired. A loan that ended because the tool was recorded lost no longer counts.
    • This also stops a holder collecting a tool set aside for them.
  • INV-CHK-6: The due date is set at checkout: the checkout date plus the loan period.
    • The loan period is the tool's default checkout period, unless the neighbor chooses a shorter one. It is never longer than the default.
    • A shorter period is chosen as a whole number of days, at least 1.
  • INV-CHK-7: A suspended neighbor can't check out a tool, and neither can a neighbor whose account is closed.
    • An account is suspended from Neighbor Suspended until Neighbor Reinstated, and closed for good from Neighbor Account Closed.
    • This also stops a suspended holder collecting a tool set aside for them. Their hold keeps its place, and the set-aside still lapses at the end of its collect-by date.
  • INV-CHK-8: There is no limit on how many tools one neighbor can have checked out at once.
  • INV-CHK-9: When a holder checks out the tool they hold, their hold ends, whether or not it had been fulfilled.
    • The tool is then on loan, so it is not set aside for anyone, and the next hold waits for its return. When the tool comes back, the former holder is no longer in the queue.
    • The views that show holds end it by matching the checkout's toolId and neighborId; a holder has at most one hold on a tool.
  • INV-CHK-11: The tool must have been added, and the borrower must be a registered account.
  • INV-CHK-12: Checking out with a loan ID that is already used opens no new loan.
    • A repeat with the same tool, borrower and loan period succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the loan since. A repeat with different details is refused.
    • The loan period compared is the one the loan started with: a request that leaves the period out is the same as one that sends the tool's default explicitly.

Check Out is offered on a reserved or set-aside tool to every neighbor, not only to the holder whose turn it is (Tool Catalog, INV-TCAT-11). This slice refuses anyone else with the reason (INV-CHK-3, INV-CHK-3a).

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: the cordless drill (tool D) has a 7-day default checkout period, Ana, Ben and Cara are registered, active neighbors with no overdue loans, and today is 5 October.

  • Happy path (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill from the Tool Catalog as loan L1, keeping the default period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for L1: the drill, Ana, a 7-day period, due 12 October, checked out today.
  • Shorter period chosen (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill and chooses a 3-day period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded with a 3-day period, due 8 October.
  • Shortest period (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill and chooses a 1-day period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded with a 1-day period, due 6 October.
  • Period equal to the default (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill and chooses a 7-day period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded with a 7-day period, due 12 October.
  • Period longer than the default (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill with an 8-day period
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The loan period must be a whole number of days from 1 up to this tool's default checkout period." No event is recorded.
  • Period of zero, or not whole (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill with a 0-day period, or a 2.5-day period
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The loan period must be a whole number of days from 1 up to this tool's default checkout period." No event is recorded.
  • Tool already checked out (INV-CHK-2)
    • Given: Ben has the drill on loan
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with tool-checked-out: "This tool is already checked out." No event is recorded.
  • Retired tool (INV-CHK-4)
    • Given: the drill has been retired
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with tool-retired: "This tool has been retired." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown tool (INV-CHK-11)
    • Given: no tool T9 has been added
    • When: Ana tries to check out T9
    • Then: refused with tool-not-found: "There is no such tool." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-CHK-11)
    • Given: no account N9 has been registered
    • When: a request to check out the drill for N9 arrives
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't borrow tools while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Closed account (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: Ana's account is closed
    • When: a request to check out the drill for Ana arrives
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Reinstated neighbor can borrow again (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: Ana was suspended and has been reinstated, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • Overdue loan blocks a checkout (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder on loan, due 4 October, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: refused with has-overdue-loan: "You have an overdue loan. Return it before borrowing another tool." No event is recorded.
  • A loan due today is not overdue (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder on loan, due 5 October, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • An extended loan is not overdue (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana's ladder loan was due 4 October, and Loan Extended moved it to 11 October
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • A loan ended by loss no longer blocks (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana's ladder loan was due 1 October, and Tool Lost has been recorded for it
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • Several loans at once (INV-CHK-8)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder and the hedge trimmer on loan, neither overdue, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded. Ana now has three tools on loan.
  • Holder collects a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-3, INV-CHK-9)
    • Given: Hold Fulfilled was recorded for Ben's hold on the drill with a collect-by date of 6 October, so the drill is set aside for him
    • When: Ben checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben, due 12 October. Ben's hold ends with it.
  • Holder collects on the collect-by date (INV-CHK-3)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, to collect by 5 October
    • When: Ben checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben.
  • Someone else tries to take a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-3)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, to collect by 6 October
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: refused with set-aside-for-another: "This tool is set aside for another neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Overdue holder can't collect (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, and Ben has the ladder on loan, due 2 October
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: refused with has-overdue-loan. The drill stays set aside for Ben until his collect-by date ends.
  • Suspended holder can't collect (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, and Ben is suspended
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended. His hold keeps its place.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-9)
    • Given: the drill has just been returned, Ben's hold is at the front of its queue and Cara's is behind it, and Hold Fulfilled has not yet been recorded
    • When: Ben checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben. Ben's hold ends without ever being fulfilled.
  • An early collector is out of the queue when the tool returns (INV-CHK-9, INV-CHK-3a)
    • Given: Ben checked out the drill as the front holder before his hold was fulfilled, with Cara's hold behind his. He has since returned it, and Cara's hold is still waiting.
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill again
    • Then: refused with reserved-for-another: "This tool is reserved for the next neighbor in the hold queue." No event is recorded. Cara is now at the front.
  • Someone who isn't next tries to take a reserved tool (INV-CHK-3a)
    • Given: the drill has just been returned, with Ben's hold at the front and Cara's behind it, and Hold Fulfilled has not yet been recorded
    • When: Cara tries to check out the drill, and then Ana does
    • Then: both are refused with reserved-for-another: "This tool is reserved for the next neighbor in the hold queue." No event is recorded.
  • Holder too late, another hold waiting (INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben on 14 October, to collect by 17 October, and Cara's hold is waiting. Hold Expired has not yet been recorded.
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill on 18 October
    • Then: refused with pickup-window-ended: "Your pickup window has ended, and this tool has passed to the next neighbor in the queue." No event is recorded. Cara can check the drill out.
  • Someone else tries a lapsed set-aside while a hold waits (INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: as above, on 18 October, before Hold Expired is recorded
    • When: Ana, who has no hold on the drill, tries to check it out
    • Then: refused with reserved-for-another. No event is recorded.
  • Next holder takes a lapsed set-aside before the expiry is recorded (INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: as above, on 18 October, before Hold Expired is recorded
    • When: Cara checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Cara, and her hold ends. Ben's hold still gets its Hold Expired.
  • Lapsed set-aside, no hold waiting, taken by someone else (INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben, to collect by 17 October, no other hold is waiting, and Hold Expired has not yet been recorded
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 18 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana. Ben's hold still gets its Hold Expired.
  • Lapsed set-aside, no hold waiting, taken by the former holder (INV-CHK-3b, INV-CHK-9)
    • Given: as above
    • When: Ben checks out the drill on 18 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben. His own checkout ends his hold, so no Hold Expired follows for it.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-CHK-12)
    • Given: Tool Checked Out was recorded for loan L1: the drill, Ana, default period
    • When: the same Check Out Tool request for L1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. Ana still has one loan of the drill.
  • A loan ID reused for different details (INV-CHK-12)
    • Given: Tool Checked Out was recorded for loan L1: the drill, Ana
    • When: a Check Out Tool request for L1 arrives naming the ladder
    • Then: refused with loan-id-in-use: "That loan ID is already used by another loan." No event is recorded.
  • Someone checks out a tool for another neighbor (INV-CHK-1)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: a request to check out the drill for Ana comes from someone other than Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only check out tools for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • No sign-in (INV-CHK-1)
    • Given: a caller with no sign-in
    • When: they ask to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on the Tool Catalog screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in, then requester-mismatch (INV-CHK-1).
  2. The loan ID is already used (INV-CHK-12): a repeat with the same details succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise loan-id-in-use.
  3. tool-not-found, then neighbor-not-found (INV-CHK-11).
  4. tool-retired (INV-CHK-4).
  5. tool-checked-out (INV-CHK-2).
  6. account-closed, then neighbor-suspended (INV-CHK-7).
  7. has-overdue-loan (INV-CHK-5).
  8. The tool's holds (INV-CHK-3, INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-3b):
    • set-aside-for-another: the tool is set aside and its collect-by date hasn't ended, and the requester isn't the holder.
    • pickup-window-ended: the set-aside's collect-by date has ended, another hold is waiting, and the requester is the former holder.
    • reserved-for-another: the tool is back with a hold waiting (or a lapsed set-aside with one waiting), and the requester isn't the neighbor at the front of the queue. This includes a third neighbor after a set-aside lapses.
  9. period-out-of-range (INV-CHK-6).
Reason Sentence Rule
loan-id-in-use That loan ID is already used by another loan. INV-CHK-12
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-CHK-1
requester-mismatch You can only check out tools for yourself. INV-CHK-1
tool-not-found There is no such tool. INV-CHK-11
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-CHK-11
tool-retired This tool has been retired. INV-CHK-4
tool-checked-out This tool is already checked out. INV-CHK-2
account-closed This account is closed. INV-CHK-7
neighbor-suspended You can't borrow tools while your account is suspended. INV-CHK-7
has-overdue-loan You have an overdue loan. Return it before borrowing another tool. INV-CHK-5
set-aside-for-another This tool is set aside for another neighbor. INV-CHK-3
pickup-window-ended Your pickup window has ended, and this tool has passed to the next neighbor in the queue. INV-CHK-3b
reserved-for-another This tool is reserved for the next neighbor in the hold queue. INV-CHK-3a
period-out-of-range The loan period must be a whole number of days from 1 up to this tool's default checkout period. INV-CHK-6

loan-id-in-use, tool-not-found and neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same loan ID and the same tool, borrower and requested period succeeds and records nothing new, even if the loan has since been extended, returned or lost. So a retry after a lost response never opens a second loan.

Two neighbors checking out the same tool at the same moment: only one Tool Checked Out is recorded for the tool. The other request is refused with tool-checked-out, because each checkout is decided against the tool's loans as already recorded, one at a time.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may check out a tool only for themselves (INV-CHK-1); the shed manager doesn't check tools out. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; requester-mismatch means it isn't the neighborId in the request.
  • PII & compliance: Tool Checked Out links a neighbor to a tool and a due date. It holds no name or email; those stay on Neighbor Registered and Neighbor Email Changed.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Tool Checked Out (this slice): loanId, toolId, neighborId, loanPeriodDays, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor), Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor), Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId. Queue order is the order these events were recorded.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • These keys match slices/add-tool.md, tool-inventory.md, tool-catalog.md and register-neighbor.md. Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate is the Date the fulfiller records (set by the system, as dueDate is on loans). Those slices aren't yet written in depth, and each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, My Loans, My Holds, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Holds To Fulfill, Pickup Notices To Send, Pickups To Expire and Neighbors To Flag. Extend Loan, Return Tool and Record Tool Lost act on the loan by its loan ID.

Open Questions

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v2: reworded; Check Out Tool no longer feeds the merged Neighbors view, Return Tool does (2026-11-01)

Slice: Return Tool

Intent

Let a borrower bring a tool back and end their loan themselves, from My Loans. The tool is then back in the shed, for the next holder or for anyone to borrow. The return records whether it was late, which is what counts toward a neighbor being flagged.

Trigger & Actor

The borrower, from their own My Loans screen, for one of their own loans. My Loans offers Return on every loan it lists (INV-MYL-12), including overdue loans, loans whose tool was retired while out, and loans of a suspended neighbor. The shed manager does not record returns; a tool that never comes back is recorded lost instead (Record Tool Lost).

Command / Input

Command: Return Tool

A NeighborId or LoanId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor returning, who must be the one making the request and the loan's borrower (INV-RET-1).
loanId LoanId yes The loan to end. Must be a loan that has been checked out (INV-RET-11), and still out (INV-RET-2).

There is no field for the tool's condition: nothing about it is recorded on return. A damaged tool is the shed manager's to retire.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Loans @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Returned → context Loans Read by: My Loans (the loan drops off), Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (the tool is back in the shed), Holds To Fulfill (a returned tool with holds waiting), Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices (the loan has ended), and Neighbors To Flag and Neighbors (whether the return was late, and the late return behind a flag).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command.
toolId ToolId yes The loan's tool, from its Tool Checked Out. Carried so views about tools and holds match on the tool directly.
toolName Text yes Set by the system: the tool's name on the loan's Tool Checked Out.
dueDate Date yes Set by the system: the loan's due date in force at the moment of return (Tool Checked Out.dueDate, moved by any Loan Extended), the date late was judged against.
returnedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.
returnedOn Date yes Set by the system: the calendar date of returnedAt in the shed's local time zone.
late Bool yes Set by the system: yes when returnedOn is after the loan's due date in force at the moment of return (INV-RET-4).

The event never changes. returnedOn and late are worked out once, by the command's handler, so every view reads the same answer.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Returned ends the loan in My Loans, Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices; puts the tool back in the shed on Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (or drops a tool retired while out); adds a tool with holds waiting to Holds To Fulfill; and gives Neighbors To Flag and Neighbors a late or on-time return. Each is specified in its own doc, and all are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

Once a loan is returned, no overdue notice goes out for it (INV-OLN-4, Overdue Loans To Notify). A returned tool with no holds waiting is available to borrow straight away; one with holds waiting is reserved, and until Hold Fulfilled is recorded only the neighbor at the front of the queue may check it out (INV-CHK-3a, Check Out Tool). Late returns count toward a neighbor being flagged, 3 within 90 days (Neighbors To Flag). Those rules are owned by those slices.

  • INV-RET-1: The borrower returns their own loan themselves, from My Loans.
    • The request must come from the neighbor it names, and the loan must be theirs. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch. The shed manager does not record returns.
  • INV-RET-2: Only a loan that is still out can be returned, and only once.
    • A loan ended by the shed manager recording the tool lost can't be returned.
    • A closed account never has a loan out, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan (INV-CLS-7, Close Account).
  • INV-RET-3: Returning a tool records only Tool Returned.
    • Setting the tool aside for the first waiting hold is a separate system reaction to the return, recorded as Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold).
  • INV-RET-4: A return is late when it happens after the loan's due date: from the start of the day after the due date, in the shed's local time.
    • A return on the due date itself is on time. The due date is the one in force at the moment of return: the latest Loan Extended's dueDate, or Tool Checked Out's if never extended.
    • Tool Returned records the answer as late, with the date of return as returnedOn.
  • INV-RET-5: An overdue loan can be returned.
  • INV-RET-7: A suspended neighbor can return a tool.
  • INV-RET-9: A tool retired while on loan can still be returned.
    • The return ends the loan as usual. The tool stays retired: it doesn't come back into the Tool Catalog or Tool Inventory, and no hold is waiting on it, because retiring it ended its holds.
  • INV-RET-10: Returning a loan that this borrower has already returned succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second return.
  • INV-RET-11: The loan must have been checked out.
  • INV-RET-12: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: on-time return, no holds (INV-RET-1, INV-RET-3, INV-RET-4)
    • Given: Ana (N1) has the cordless drill (T1) on loan L1, due 12 October, and no holds are waiting on it
    • When: at 15:00 on 11 October, shed time, Ana returns L1 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L1, with toolId T1, the time it was recorded, returnedOn 11 October, and late no. Nothing else is recorded.
  • Return on the due date (INV-RET-4)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Ana returns L1 at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with returnedOn 12 October, late no.
  • Late return (INV-RET-4, INV-RET-5)
    • Given: L1 was due 12 October, and Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for it
    • When: Ana returns L1 at 00:05 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with returnedOn 13 October, late yes.
  • Return after an extension (INV-RET-4)
    • Given: L1 was due 12 October, and Loan Extended moved its due date to 19 October
    • When: Ana returns L1 on 15 October
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with late no, judged against 19 October.
  • Return with a hold waiting (INV-RET-3)
    • Given: Ana has L1, and Ben's hold on T1 is at the front of the queue
    • When: Ana returns L1
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded. No Hold Fulfilled is recorded by this command; setting T1 aside for Ben is Fulfill Hold's.
  • Suspended neighbor returns a tool (INV-RET-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended and has L1 out
    • When: Ana returns L1 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L1.
  • Returning a tool that was retired while on loan (INV-RET-9)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder (T2) on loan L2, and Tool Retired was recorded for T2 while it was out
    • When: Ana returns L2 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L2, with toolId T2. T2 stays retired.
  • The same return twice (INV-RET-10)
    • Given: Tool Returned was recorded for L1
    • When: Ana's same Return Tool request for L1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Loan already recorded lost (INV-RET-2)
    • Given: Tool Lost was recorded for Ana's loan L3
    • When: Ana asks to return L3
    • Then: refused with loan-ended: "This loan has ended." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else's loan (INV-RET-1)
    • Given: Ana has L1 out
    • When: Ben asks, for himself, to return L1
    • Then: refused with not-your-loan: "You can only return your own loans." No event is recorded.
  • A request in someone else's name (INV-RET-1)
    • Given: Ana has L1 out
    • When: a request from Ben asks to return L1 for Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only return loans for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown loan (INV-RET-11)
    • Given: no loan has ID L9
    • When: Ana asks to return L9
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-RET-12)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for returning a tool arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the borrower on the My Loans screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-RET-12): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-RET-1).
  3. loan-not-found (INV-RET-11).
  4. not-your-loan (INV-RET-1).
  5. If Tool Returned is already recorded for the loan, the request is a repeat: it succeeds and records nothing (INV-RET-10).
  6. loan-ended, if Tool Lost is recorded for the loan (INV-RET-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-RET-12
requester-mismatch You can only return loans for yourself. INV-RET-1
loan-not-found There is no such loan. INV-RET-11
not-your-loan You can only return your own loans. INV-RET-1
loan-ended This loan has ended. INV-RET-2

requester-mismatch and loan-not-found can only come from a faulty or impersonating caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. The names mean the same conditions as in Extend Loan, and loan-ended uses the same sentence.

Suspension, an overdue loan and a retired tool never stop a return; there is no refusal for them.

Idempotency: a return is identified by its loan. A repeat after the loan was returned succeeds and records nothing. A loan ended by Tool Lost is refused, because returning it would be a different outcome from the one recorded.

Requests at the same moment: each Return Tool is decided against the loan's events as already recorded, one at a time per loan. Of a return and a Record Tool Lost for the same loan at once, whichever is decided first is recorded; the other finds the loan ended (a return then gets loan-ended, or succeeds as a repeat if the first was itself a return).

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a borrower may return only their own loans (INV-RET-1); the shed manager doesn't record returns. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • PII & compliance: Tool Returned holds no name or email; it records which loan ended, when, and whether it was late.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (this slice): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • These match slices/check-out-tool.md and slices/extend-loan.md. Record Tool Lost is specified in a slice not yet written in depth; it is checked against this key when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Loans, Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, Holds To Fulfill, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Neighbors To Flag and Neighbors. Fulfill Hold reacts to a returned tool with holds waiting.

Open Questions

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v2: reworded; Check Out Tool no longer feeds the merged Neighbors view, Return Tool does (2026-11-01)
