    2. Each recorded Pickup Notice Sent is handed to the provider from the event itself, using the hold ID as the hand-off's key. The hand-off is driven by the recorded event, not by the list: if the hand-off call errors, or the process stops before the provider accepts, it is repeated with the same key (after a restart too) until the provider accepts it. This is an outbox, not a domain event.
  • The email: to the address recorded on the event, giving the holder's name, the tool's name and the collect-by date recorded on it, and saying that the hold expires and the tool passes to the next neighbor if it isn't collected by then (INV-PKN-3, INV-PKN-7).
  • The email port's contract, from the shed's house rules, is the same as for overdue notices: the provider accepts a hand-off with a key, sends at most one email per key, makes its own delivery attempts (3 over about an hour), and sends one final failure report quoting the key, signed so the shed can trust it. A final failure is recorded by Record Pickup Notice Failure (slices/record-pickup-notice-failure.md). The hold still shows as ready for pickup, and the pickup window runs as usual.

Command / Input

Command: Send Pickup Notice

A HoldId is a UUID. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone. "Today" is that date at the moment the command is handled.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
holdId HoldId yes The set-aside hold. Must be a hold that has been placed (INV-PKN-9) and fulfilled (INV-PKN-10), whose set-aside hasn't ended (INV-PKN-5) and whose collect-by date hasn't passed (INV-PKN-12).
sentTo Text yes The address to send to: the holder's current email, from the list item's holderEmail.
holderName Text yes From the list item. Shown in the email.
toolName Text yes From the list item. Shown in the email.
collectByDate Date yes From the list item. Must be the hold's collect-by date as recorded on Hold Fulfilled (INV-PKN-11). Shown in the email.

Trigger

Triggered by: translation Pickup Notice Gateway, also in this slice, reading Pickup Notices To Send.

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Pickup Notice Sent → context Holds Read by: Pickup Notices To Send (the hold leaves the list for good) and My Holds (shows the holder that they were emailed).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
holdId HoldId yes From the command. Also the key of the hand-off, which the provider's failure report quotes back.
sentTo Text yes From the command: the address the email went to.
holderName Text yes From the command: the name the email was addressed to.
toolName Text yes From the command: the tool named in the email.
collectByDate Date yes From the command: the collect-by date the email gave.
sentAt Instant yes Set by the system: the UTC moment the event is recorded.

The address, name, tool name and collect-by date are facts of the email: what was actually sent. They are recorded on the event so the hand-off can be repeated, even after a restart, without the list, and so they don't change if the neighbor's details change later. Outgoing-email events are the one kind of event that carries copies of names.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. The gateway reads Pickup Notices To Send, specified in slices/pickup-notices-to-send.md. Pickup Notice Sent removes the hold from that list and marks it on My Holds. Both are eventually consistent: the list may still show a hold for a moment after its email is recorded, which is why the command itself refuses a second email.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-PKN-2: At most one pickup email is sent per set-aside.
    • Once Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for a hold, it is never emailed again.
    • A repeated Send Pickup Notice with the same content succeeds and records nothing, and nothing new is handed over. One with different content is refused.
  • INV-PKN-3: Pickup emails go by email only, through the same provider as overdue notices, to the holder's current email address.
    • Neighbor Registered sets it, Neighbor Email Changed replaces it. The address used is the one recorded on Pickup Notice Sent. An email change after that doesn't resend the email or change where a pending hand-off goes.
  • INV-PKN-4: Pickup Notice Sent is recorded before the email is handed to the email provider, and every email handed over has one.
    • The hand-off is driven from the recorded event and repeated with the same key, after a restart too, until the provider accepts it. That is a technical retry, not a failure of the email.
    • Pickup Notice Sent doesn't mean the holder received or read the email. Any failure the provider reports later follows this Pickup Notice Sent.
  • INV-PKN-5: No pickup email is sent for a set-aside that has already ended.
    • A set-aside ends when its hold ends: the holder checks the tool out, the hold is cancelled or expires, the tool is retired, or the holder closes their account.
  • INV-PKN-6: The email goes out as soon as the tool is set aside, with no quiet hours.
    • The pickup window starts at the set-aside, not when the email is sent; the collect-by date doesn't move.
  • INV-PKN-7: The email gives the holder's name, the tool's name, the collect-by date, and that the hold expires and the tool passes to the next neighbor if it isn't collected by then.
    • Its subject line is "Your is ready for pickup".
  • INV-PKN-9: The hold must exist.
  • INV-PKN-10: The hold must have been fulfilled: a waiting hold gets no pickup email.
  • INV-PKN-11: The collect-by date given must be the one recorded on the hold's Hold Fulfilled.
  • INV-PKN-12: No pickup email is sent once the collect-by date has passed, even if Hold Expired hasn't been recorded yet.
    • The set-aside lapses at the start of the day after the collect-by date, shed local time. An email sent after that would tell the holder to collect by a date that is already over.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ben Ito (ben@example.org) holds the cordless drill under hold H1, and Hold Fulfilled was recorded for H1 on 14 October with a collect-by date of 17 October. Today is 14 October in the shed's local time.

  • Happy path (INV-PKN-6, INV-PKN-7)
    • Given: H1 joined Pickup Notices To Send when Hold Fulfilled was recorded
    • When: the gateway issues Send Pickup Notice for H1, to ben@example.org, for Ben Ito, the cordless drill, collect by 17 October
    • Then: Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for H1 with that address, name, tool name and collect-by date. The gateway then hands the provider an email to ben@example.org, keyed H1, telling Ben Ito the cordless drill is ready for him, to collect by 17 October, and that otherwise his hold expires and the drill passes to the next neighbor.
  • The gateway reads the same hold twice (INV-PKN-2)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent has been recorded for H1, and the list returned H1 once more before it caught up
    • When: the gateway issues the same Send Pickup Notice for H1 again
    • Then: the command succeeds and records nothing new. Nothing new is handed over, so Ben gets one email.
  • A repeat with different content (INV-PKN-2)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent has been recorded for H1 to ben@example.org
    • When: a Send Pickup Notice for H1 arrives giving ben.ito@example.net
    • Then: refused with notice-already-sent: "A pickup email has already been sent for this hold." No event is recorded, and nothing is handed over.
  • The process stops before the provider accepts (INV-PKN-4)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent has been recorded for H1, and the process stopped before the hand-off was accepted. H1 has already left Pickup Notices To Send.
    • When: the gateway starts again
    • Then: it hands the email over from the recorded Pickup Notice Sent, keyed H1, to ben@example.org with the recorded content. One email goes out.
  • The hand-off call errors (INV-PKN-4)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent has been recorded for H1, and the first hand-off call fails with a connection error
    • When: the gateway repeats the hand-off, keyed H1, and the provider accepts it
    • Then: one email goes to ben@example.org. Nothing more is recorded.
  • Holder collected before the email went out (INV-PKN-5)
    • Given: Ben checked out the drill before the gateway acted, which ended H1, and the list hasn't caught up yet
    • When: the gateway issues Send Pickup Notice for H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended: "This hold has already ended." No event is recorded, and nothing is handed over.
  • Hold cancelled before the email went out (INV-PKN-5)
    • Given: Ben cancelled H1 before the gateway acted
    • When: the gateway issues Send Pickup Notice for H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Hold expired before the email went out (INV-PKN-5)
    • Given: Hold Expired has been recorded for H1, and no pickup email was sent
    • When: a Send Pickup Notice for H1 arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Tool retired, or holder's account closed, before the email went out (INV-PKN-5)
    • Given: the drill was retired while set aside for Ben
    • When: the gateway issues Send Pickup Notice for H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded. The same applies if Ben closed his account instead.
  • Current email used (INV-PKN-3)
    • Given: Ben changed his email to ben.ito@example.net before H1 was fulfilled
    • When: the gateway issues Send Pickup Notice for H1 with the list's current address
    • Then: Pickup Notice Sent is recorded with sentTo ben.ito@example.net, and the email goes there.
  • Email changed after the email was recorded (INV-PKN-3)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent was recorded for H1 to ben@example.org, and its hand-off hasn't been accepted yet
    • When: Ben changes his email to ben.ito@example.net
    • Then: the email still goes to ben@example.org, the address recorded on it.
  • A waiting hold (INV-PKN-10)
    • Given: Cara's hold H2 on the drill is waiting, not fulfilled
    • When: a Send Pickup Notice for H2 arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-not-set-aside: "This hold hasn't been set aside." No event is recorded.
  • Wrong collect-by date (INV-PKN-11)
    • Given: H1's collect-by date is 17 October
    • When: a Send Pickup Notice for H1 arrives giving 18 October
    • Then: refused with collect-by-date-mismatch: "This isn't the hold's collect-by date." No event is recorded.
  • Collect-by date already passed (INV-PKN-12)
    • Given: H1's collect-by date is 17 October, no pickup email has been sent, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded. Today is 18 October.
    • When: a Send Pickup Notice for H1 arrives
    • Then: refused with pickup-window-ended: "This set-aside's pickup window has ended." No event is recorded, and nothing is handed over.
  • Unknown hold (INV-PKN-9)
    • Given: no hold H9 has been placed
    • When: a Send Pickup Notice for H9 arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-not-found: "There is no such hold." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

A refusal records nothing, and the gateway hands nothing over for that hold. No person sees these reasons; they are logged with the hold ID. The name is the contract; the sentence is the log text.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. hold-not-found (INV-PKN-9).
  2. If Pickup Notice Sent is already recorded for the hold: with the same address, name, tool name and collect-by date, the command succeeds and records nothing; otherwise notice-already-sent (INV-PKN-2).
  3. hold-ended (INV-PKN-5).
  4. hold-not-set-aside (INV-PKN-10).
  5. collect-by-date-mismatch (INV-PKN-11).
  6. pickup-window-ended (INV-PKN-12).
Reason Sentence Rule
hold-not-found There is no such hold. INV-PKN-9
notice-already-sent A pickup email has already been sent for this hold. INV-PKN-2
hold-ended This hold has already ended. INV-PKN-5
hold-not-set-aside This hold hasn't been set aside. INV-PKN-10
collect-by-date-mismatch This isn't the hold's collect-by date. INV-PKN-11
pickup-window-ended This set-aside's pickup window has ended. INV-PKN-12

hold-not-found and hold-ended mean the same conditions as in Cancel Hold and Fulfill Hold; notice-already-sent the same as in Send Overdue Notice; pickup-window-ended the same as in Check Out Tool (the set-aside's collect-by date has passed). hold-not-set-aside and collect-by-date-mismatch can only come from a stale list or a faulty caller. A missing or malformed hold ID (not a UUID), or a blank sentTo, holderName or toolName, is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated Send Pickup Notice for a hold that already has its Pickup Notice Sent, with the same content, succeeds and records nothing, and nothing new is handed over. Emails are handed over only from recorded Pickup Notice Sent events.

Hand-off retries: the hand-off is driven from each recorded Pickup Notice Sent until the provider accepts it. A call that errors, or a stop before acceptance, is repeated with the same key, the hold ID, after a restart too. The provider sends at most one email per key. Delivery attempts after acceptance are the provider's; a final failure is recorded by Record Pickup Notice Failure.

Requests at the same moment: Send Pickup Notice is decided against the hold's events as already recorded, one at a time per hold, so at most one Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for a hold.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: Send Pickup Notice is internal. Only the Pickup Notice Gateway issues it; it is not exposed to neighbors or the shed manager.
  • PII & compliance: the email carries the holder's name, email address and the tool set aside for them. Pickup Notice Sent records the same, as facts of the email that was sent. Names and emails are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: the email is recorded within moments of Hold Fulfilled, and handed over as soon as the provider accepts it.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, collectByDate.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): toolId, neighborId (the holder's own checkout ends the hold).
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Pickup Notice Sent (this slice): holdId, sentTo, holderName, toolName, collectByDate.
    • The gateway reads Pickup Notices To Send's items: holdId, holderEmail, holderName, toolName, collectByDate (slices/pickup-notices-to-send.md).
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs and the Hold Fulfilled convention.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Pickup Notices To Send (the hold leaves it) and My Holds (shows the email was sent). Record Pickup Notice Failure matches the provider's failure report to the hold by the hand-off key, the hold ID.

Open Questions

  • Bad input: blank sentTo, holderName or toolName is rejected as bad input; the email subject is 'Your is ready for pickup' (conformance 2026-11-01, finding 7) — v2: bad input stated under Alternate & Error Flows, the subject line under INV-PKN-7 (2026-11-01)
"},{"index":22,"name":"My Holds — pickup notice sent","x0":3838.76,"x1":3982.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: My Holds

Intent

Shows a neighbor the holds they have, on the My Holds screen: where they stand in each tool's queue, and when a tool has been set aside for them, the date to collect it by and whether the pickup email reached them. It is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is waiting for them, and the screen they cancel holds from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Holds screen.
  • Whose holds it shows: the holds of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its one action issues a command owned by another slice:
    • Cancel (Cancel Hold slice) — offered on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).
    • A neighbor collects a set-aside tool with an ordinary checkout from the Tool Catalog, not from here.

Read Model / View

  • View: My Holds built from events: "Hold Placed", "Tool Checked Out", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Fulfilled", "Pickup Notice Sent", "Pickup Notice Failed", "Hold Expired", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the My Holds screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a set-aside's pickup window has ended is worked out when the view is read, from collectByDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it is always current. No action on this screen depends on the view being instant, because Cancel Hold and Check Out Tool each check their own rules when they run.

One row per hold that hasn't ended. HoldId, ToolId, LoanId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

Field Type Source / Notes
holdId HoldId Hold Placed.holdId.
neighborId NeighborId Hold Placed.neighborId: the holder.
toolId ToolId Hold Placed.toolId.
toolName Text Hold Placed.toolName (INV-MYHD-14).
placedAt Instant Hold Placed.placedAt. For display only; it doesn't decide the queue.
status Text One of waiting, ready-for-pickup, pickup-window-ended. Derived: see the status rules below.
position Int Derived: while status is waiting, 1 plus the number of this tool's holds that are waiting, were placed before this one, and haven't ended (INV-MYHD-2). Optional: absent once the hold is fulfilled.
collectByDate Date Derived: Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate for this hold, read as recorded, never worked out here (INV-MYHD-3). Optional: absent while waiting.
pickupNotice Text One of none, sent, undelivered. Derived: sent once Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for this hold, undelivered once Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for it, none before either (INV-MYHD-13).
canCancel Bool Derived: yes on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).

Status rules. A hold's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. pickup-window-ended — Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold, and today's date in the shed's local time zone is after its collectByDate (INV-MYHD-17).
  2. ready-for-pickup — otherwise, Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold.
  3. waiting — otherwise.

When a hold leaves the view. A hold is listed from Hold Placed until it ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, when the holder checks the tool out, when the tool is retired or recorded lost, or when the holder closes their account. In events:

  • Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for the hold;
  • Tool Checked Out for the hold's tool by the hold's neighbor;
  • Tool Retired or Tool Lost for the hold's tool;
  • Neighbor Account Closed for the holder.

Queue order. A tool's queue is the order in which Hold Placed was recorded for it. To work out positions, the view keeps, for each tool, every hold on it that hasn't ended, with its holder and whether it has been fulfilled. This is bookkeeping, not part of the row, and other neighbors' holds are never returned.

Queries

  • List my holds. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns every hold of that neighbor that hasn't ended, each with every field above, and nothing about anyone else's holds (INV-MYHD-1). There is no paging. A neighbor with no holds gets an empty list. Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when the hold was placed, in the order Hold Placed was recorded (INV-MYHD-18).

Invariants / Business Rules

A neighbor has at most one hold on any one tool, because Place Hold refuses a second (INV-HOLD-7, Place Hold). A suspended neighbor can't place a new hold (INV-HOLD-9) or collect a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-7), but may still cancel. An expired hold sends no message, doesn't count against the neighbor, and the neighbor may place a new hold on the tool at the back of the queue (Expire Hold). A suspended neighbor keeps their holds and their place in each queue. A front holder who can't collect, because they are suspended or have an overdue loan, still has the tool set aside for them, and the pickup window runs regardless (Fulfill Hold, INV-FUL-8). These rules are owned by those slices; this view just reflects the events they record, and it doesn't hear suspension or loans at all (INV-MYHD-11).

  • INV-MYHD-1: A neighbor's My Holds shows only their own holds.
    • The query returns only holds whose holder is the neighbor ID it is given. It never shows who else holds a tool, only the neighbor's own position. No neighbor-facing screen ever shows who has a tool or who holds one; only the shed manager sees borrowers, on Tool Inventory.
  • INV-MYHD-2: Holds on a tool queue in the order they were placed. Each waiting hold shows the neighbor's position in that tool's queue.
    • Position 1 is the next hold to be fulfilled. A hold moves up as holds ahead of it are fulfilled or end.
    • A hold that has been fulfilled is no longer in the waiting queue, so the first waiting hold behind a set-aside is at position 1.
  • INV-MYHD-3: Once a neighbor's hold is fulfilled, My Holds shows the tool as ready for pickup, with the date to collect it by.
    • The collect-by date is the one Hold Fulfilled carries: the date the tool was set aside plus 3 days. My Holds shows it as recorded and never works it out itself.
    • My Holds is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is set aside for them. The Tool Catalog is the same for every neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-4: A hold that is ready for pickup stays on My Holds until the holder collects it, cancels it, or Hold Expired is recorded for it. Then it drops off.
    • The tool then passes to the next hold, which shows as ready for pickup on that neighbor's My Holds once Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • INV-MYHD-5: When a holder checks out the tool they hold, their hold ends and drops off My Holds, whether or not it had been fulfilled.
    • The loan then appears on My Loans.
  • INV-MYHD-6: A cancelled hold drops off My Holds, whether it was waiting or ready for pickup.
    • Cancelling a hold that is ready for pickup passes the tool to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-7: Retiring a tool, or recording it lost, ends every hold on it, and those holds drop off My Holds.
    • The holders are not told.
  • INV-MYHD-8: Closing an account ends all of that neighbor's holds. Their holds drop off My Holds, and holds behind them move up.
    • A tool that was ready for pickup for them passes to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-13: Once a tool is set aside for a neighbor, My Holds shows whether the pickup email was sent or couldn't be delivered.
    • If the email can't be delivered, the tool stays ready for pickup, with the same collect-by date.
  • INV-MYHD-14: Each hold shows the tool's name.
    • The name comes with Hold Placed, which carries it.
  • INV-MYHD-11: Only Hold Placed, Hold Cancelled, Hold Fulfilled, Pickup Notice Sent, Pickup Notice Failed, Hold Expired, Tool Checked Out by a holder of that tool, Tool Retired, Tool Lost and Neighbor Account Closed change My Holds.
    • A checkout by anyone else leaves every neighbor's My Holds unchanged.
  • INV-MYHD-15: Applying the same event twice leaves My Holds as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYHD-16: My Holds offers Cancel on every hold it lists.
    • That includes holds ready for pickup, holds whose pickup window has ended, and holds of a suspended neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-17: Once a set-aside's collect-by date has passed, My Holds shows that the pickup window has ended, even before Hold Expired is recorded.
    • From the start of the day after the collect-by date, in the shed's local time, the set-aside is no longer theirs: the tool goes to the next neighbor in the queue, or to whoever checks it out first if nobody is waiting (INV-CHK-3b, Check Out Tool). The hold drops off when Hold Expired is recorded.
  • INV-MYHD-18: Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when they were placed.
  • INV-MYHD-19: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYHD-20: My Holds is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Hold placed (INV-MYHD-2, INV-MYHD-14, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ana has T1, the "Cordless drill", on loan, and nobody has a hold on it
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on T1, carrying the name "Cordless drill"
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H1: "Cordless drill", waiting, position 1, pickup notice none, with Cancel offered.
  • A second hold placed (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Cara's My Holds lists H2, waiting, position 2. Ben's is unchanged.
  • Holds placed in the same instant (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's H2 and then Dan's H3 on T1, with the same placedAt
    • Then: H2 is at position 2 and H3 at position 3: the order recorded decides, not placedAt.
  • Hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has been returned
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, with the collect-by date 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, with no position. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Pickup email sent (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, pickup notice none
    • When: Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice sent.
  • Pickup email couldn't be delivered (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, pickup notice sent
    • When: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice undelivered, still ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Collect-by date is the last day (INV-MYHD-17)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October
    • When: his holds are listed at 23:59 on 17 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 is ready-for-pickup.
  • Pickup window ended, not yet expired (INV-MYHD-17, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded
    • When: his holds are listed at 00:00 on 18 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 shows pickup-window-ended, with Cancel still offered.
  • Hold expired (INV-MYHD-4)
    • Given: Ben's H1 shows pickup-window-ended, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting at position 1 until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Suspended holder (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-11)
    • Given: Ben is suspended, and his H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: T1 is returned and Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, collect by 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Holder collects the tool (INV-MYHD-5)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Ben
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's is unchanged.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-MYHD-5, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has just been returned
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Ben, before Hold Fulfilled
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Ready-for-pickup hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Tool retired (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for T1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan as loan L1, and Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L1, the loan of T1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-MYHD-8)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ben
    • Then: H1 drops off. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold again after expiry (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 expired, and T1 is now set aside for Cara's H2
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's new hold H4 on T1
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H4, waiting, position 1, behind Cara's set-aside.
  • Checkout by a neighbor with no hold (INV-MYHD-11)
    • Given: Ana has no holds, and the hammer (T5) is available
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T5 and Ana
    • Then: no neighbor's My Holds changes.
  • Only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1)
    • Given: Ben has H1 and Cara has H2, both on T1
    • When: Ben's holds are listed
    • Then: only H1 is returned, with its position. Nothing about H2 or Cara is returned.
  • List order (INV-MYHD-18)
    • Given: Ben placed H5 on the ladder, then H1 on the cordless drill
    • When: his holds are listed
    • Then: H1 (cordless drill) comes first, then H5 (ladder).
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYHD-15)
    • Given: Ben's My Holds lists H1 at position 1
    • When: the same Hold Placed for H1 is applied again
    • Then: Ben's My Holds still lists H1 once, at position 1, and no later hold's position changes.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYHD-19)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Holds is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYHD-20)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: the holds of N1, Ana, are asked for
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own holds." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-MYHD-19
requester-mismatch You can only see your own holds. INV-MYHD-20
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYHD-15). An event applied a second time leaves the view as it was after the first.
  • Events for a hold that has ended: once a hold has ended it is gone from this view. A later event for it (a replay, or a Pickup Notice Failed that arrives after the set-aside ended) changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: Cancel offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, just as the hold expires or the tool is collected). Cancel Hold checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may list only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  • PII & compliance: shows a neighbor their own holds only, and never who else holds or has a tool. The other holders and borrowers it keeps for working out positions are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, placedAt.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Pickup Notice Sent (Send Pickup Notice): holdId.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (Record Pickup Notice Failure): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId. This view matches it by toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Hold Placed and Tool Checked Out match slices/place-hold.md and slices/check-out-tool.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Cancel Hold.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":23,"name":"Record Pickup Notice Failure","x0":4015.76,"x1":4159.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Record Pickup Notice Failure

Intent

Record that a pickup email could not be delivered to the holder, so the shed manager can see the neighbor wasn't told their tool is ready and can let them know another way, and the holder's My Holds shows that the email didn't reach them.

Trigger & Actor

Externally triggered. The email provider, outside the shed, sends a final failure report for a pickup email the shed handed it. The Pickup Email Failure Report translation turns that report into the Record Pickup Notice Failure command. No person records a failure, and there is no screen.

What the report carries: the reference the shed gave the email when it handed it over, which is the hold's ID, since each set-aside gets at most one pickup email; and the reason, refused or bounced. Anything else in the report, such as the email address, is not recorded. A report whose reference is a loan's ID is about an overdue notice: it belongs to Record Overdue Notice Failure, and this translation drops it without issuing a command.

Command / Input

Command: Record Pickup Notice Failure

A HoldId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
holdId HoldId yes The reference from the provider's report: the hold the email was about. Must match a Pickup Notice Sent (INV-PNF-8), for a set-aside that hasn't ended (INV-PNF-9).
reason Text yes refused or bounced, from the report (INV-PNF-3). Any other value is bad input.

Trigger

Triggered by: translation Pickup Email Failure Report, also in this slice (externally triggered by the email provider's final failure report).

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Pickup Notice Failed → context Holds Read by: My Holds (the hold shows the pickup email couldn't be delivered) and Undelivered Notices (the shed manager's follow-up list).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
holdId HoldId yes From the command.
reason Text yes From the command: refused or bounced.
failedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the failure date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

The event never changes. No later event retries the email or clears the failure.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Pickup Notice Failed feeds two views, each specified in its own doc:

  • My Holds (slices/my-holds.md) shows the holder that the pickup email couldn't be delivered.
  • Undelivered Notices (slices/undelivered-notices.md) lists the failure for the shed manager, with the holder's name and email, the tool and the collect-by date, until the set-aside ends.

Both are eventually consistent. Pickup Notices To Send doesn't hear this event: the hold left that list when Pickup Notice Sent was recorded.

Invariants / Business Rules

A failure is recorded only from the email provider's report; no person records it, and the only way in is the translation in Trigger & Actor. The shed records only the provider's one final failure report: the provider makes 3 delivery attempts over about an hour and reports a final failure only if all of them fail. The shed does no retrying of its own. The provider signs each final report, under the shed's house email-port contract; the translation checks the signature and drops an unsigned or wrongly signed report without issuing any command. The provider's signature, not a sign-in, is what guards this command.

A failed pickup email changes nothing about the hold: the tool stays set aside for the holder until the end of the collect-by date, and the window isn't extended (Expire Hold owns when it ends). Every recorded failure is shown on Undelivered Notices until the set-aside ends, and on the holder's My Holds; those views own how it is shown.

  • INV-PNF-3: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for the hold the email was about, with the moment of the failure and whether the email was refused or bounced.
    • Refused and bounced are the two reasons the provider's final report can give.
  • INV-PNF-4: A set-aside has at most one Pickup Notice Failed. No further pickup email is attempted for it.
  • INV-PNF-5: Every Pickup Notice Failed follows a Pickup Notice Sent for the same hold.
    • Pickup Notice Sent is recorded at hand-off, so the hold has already left Pickup Notices To Send. Recording the failure doesn't change that list.
  • INV-PNF-8: A failure report that matches no pickup email the shed sent is ignored, and nothing is recorded.
  • INV-PNF-9: A failure report that arrives after the set-aside has ended is ignored, and nothing is recorded.
    • A set-aside ends when the holder collects the tool, the hold is cancelled or expires, the tool is retired or recorded lost, or the holder closes their account.
    • For example, the holder collected the tool during the hour the provider spent retrying.
  • INV-PNF-10: A failure report repeated for a hold whose failure is already recorded, with the same reason, succeeds and records nothing new. With a different reason it is ignored, and nothing is recorded.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Refused (INV-PNF-3)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent was recorded for Ben's hold H1 on the drill, and the set-aside hasn't ended
    • When: the provider's final report says the email for H1 was refused
    • Then: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1, reason refused, with the time it was recorded. No further pickup email is sent for H1.
  • Bounced (INV-PNF-3)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent was recorded for H1, and the set-aside hasn't ended
    • When: the provider's final report says the email for H1 bounced
    • Then: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1, reason bounced.
  • Report matching no email (INV-PNF-5, INV-PNF-8)
    • Given: no Pickup Notice Sent has been recorded for hold H2
    • When: a failure report names H2
    • Then: ignored with no-matching-notice. Nothing is recorded.
  • Report after the holder collected the tool (INV-PNF-9)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent was recorded for H1, and Ben then checked the drill out
    • When: the provider's final report says the email for H1 bounced
    • Then: ignored with hold-ended. Nothing is recorded.
  • Report after the hold expired (INV-PNF-9)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent was recorded for H1, and Hold Expired was then recorded for H1
    • When: the provider's final report says the email for H1 was refused
    • Then: ignored with hold-ended. Nothing is recorded.
  • Report after the hold was cancelled (INV-PNF-9)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent was recorded for H1, and Hold Cancelled was then recorded for H1
    • When: the provider's final report says the email for H1 bounced
    • Then: ignored with hold-ended. Nothing is recorded.
  • Report after the tool was retired (INV-PNF-9)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent was recorded for H1, and Tool Retired was then recorded for the drill
    • When: the provider's final report says the email for H1 bounced
    • Then: ignored with hold-ended. Nothing is recorded.
  • Report after the tool was recorded lost (INV-PNF-9)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent was recorded for H1, and Tool Lost was then recorded for the drill, out on another neighbor's loan
    • When: the provider's final report says the email for H1 bounced
    • Then: ignored with hold-ended. Nothing is recorded.
  • Report after the holder closed their account (INV-PNF-9)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Sent was recorded for H1, and Neighbor Account Closed was then recorded for Ben
    • When: the provider's final report says the email for H1 bounced
    • Then: ignored with hold-ended. Nothing is recorded.
  • The same report arrives twice (INV-PNF-4, INV-PNF-10)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Failed was recorded for H1, reason bounced
    • When: the same report, H1 bounced, arrives again
    • Then: it succeeds and nothing new is recorded. H1 still has one Pickup Notice Failed.
  • A second report with a different reason (INV-PNF-4, INV-PNF-10)
    • Given: Pickup Notice Failed was recorded for H1, reason bounced
    • When: a report arrives saying the email for H1 was refused
    • Then: ignored with failure-already-recorded. Nothing is recorded; H1 keeps its one failure, reason bounced.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: a stable name and a sentence. No person sees these; they go back to the translation, which takes no further action, and are kept for diagnosing the provider link.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. no-matching-notice (INV-PNF-8).
  2. A failure already recorded for the hold (INV-PNF-10): a repeat with the same reason succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise failure-already-recorded.
  3. hold-ended (INV-PNF-9).
Reason Sentence Rule
no-matching-notice No pickup email was sent for that hold. INV-PNF-8
failure-already-recorded A failure is already recorded for that email. INV-PNF-10
hold-ended This hold has already ended. INV-PNF-9

no-matching-notice and failure-already-recorded mean the same conditions as in Record Overdue Notice Failure, keyed here by hold instead of loan. A missing or malformed hold ID, or a reason other than refused or bounced, is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. A verified report keyed by a loan's ID never reaches this command: the translation drops it as an overdue-notice report (Trigger & Actor).

Idempotency: the provider may deliver the same final report more than once. A repeat with the same hold and reason succeeds and records nothing new, even if the set-aside has since ended. So one failure never shows twice on Undelivered Notices.

Retries and compensations: none in the shed. The provider's own 3 attempts happen before its final report. After a failure no further pickup email is attempted; the shed manager can let the holder know another way.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the email provider's failure report can trigger this command, through the translation. The provider signs each final report, under the shed's house email-port contract; the translation checks the signature and drops an unsigned or wrongly signed report without issuing any command. The provider's signature, not a sign-in, is what guards this command.
  • PII & compliance: Pickup Notice Failed holds no name or email: only the hold, the reason and the time. The address the email went to is already on Pickup Notice Sent, so the address in the provider's report is not recorded again.
  • Performance / SLA: none. A failure shows on Undelivered Notices shortly after the report arrives, about an hour after the email was handed over.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Pickup Notice Sent (Send Pickup Notice): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (this slice): holdId, reason.
    • Pickup Notice Sent keyed by hold ID is agreed with Send Pickup Notice. Hold Fulfilled and Tool Checked Out match the conventions and slices/check-out-tool.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Holds and Undelivered Notices (the failure).

Open Questions

  • INV-PNF-9: Tool Lost also ends a set-aside; a loan-keyed failure report is routed to Record Overdue Notice Failure, not recorded here (conformance 2026-11-01, finding 8) — v2: INV-PNF-9 lists Tool Lost, with a scenario and a Dependencies entry; the loan-keyed routing is stated under Trigger & Actor and Alternate & Error Flows (2026-11-01)
"},{"index":24,"name":"My Holds — pickup notice failed","x0":4192.76,"x1":4336.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: My Holds

Intent

Shows a neighbor the holds they have, on the My Holds screen: where they stand in each tool's queue, and when a tool has been set aside for them, the date to collect it by and whether the pickup email reached them. It is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is waiting for them, and the screen they cancel holds from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Holds screen.
  • Whose holds it shows: the holds of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its one action issues a command owned by another slice:
    • Cancel (Cancel Hold slice) — offered on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).
    • A neighbor collects a set-aside tool with an ordinary checkout from the Tool Catalog, not from here.

Read Model / View

  • View: My Holds built from events: "Hold Placed", "Tool Checked Out", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Fulfilled", "Pickup Notice Sent", "Pickup Notice Failed", "Hold Expired", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the My Holds screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a set-aside's pickup window has ended is worked out when the view is read, from collectByDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it is always current. No action on this screen depends on the view being instant, because Cancel Hold and Check Out Tool each check their own rules when they run.

One row per hold that hasn't ended. HoldId, ToolId, LoanId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

Field Type Source / Notes
holdId HoldId Hold Placed.holdId.
neighborId NeighborId Hold Placed.neighborId: the holder.
toolId ToolId Hold Placed.toolId.
toolName Text Hold Placed.toolName (INV-MYHD-14).
placedAt Instant Hold Placed.placedAt. For display only; it doesn't decide the queue.
status Text One of waiting, ready-for-pickup, pickup-window-ended. Derived: see the status rules below.
position Int Derived: while status is waiting, 1 plus the number of this tool's holds that are waiting, were placed before this one, and haven't ended (INV-MYHD-2). Optional: absent once the hold is fulfilled.
collectByDate Date Derived: Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate for this hold, read as recorded, never worked out here (INV-MYHD-3). Optional: absent while waiting.
pickupNotice Text One of none, sent, undelivered. Derived: sent once Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for this hold, undelivered once Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for it, none before either (INV-MYHD-13).
canCancel Bool Derived: yes on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).

Status rules. A hold's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. pickup-window-ended — Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold, and today's date in the shed's local time zone is after its collectByDate (INV-MYHD-17).
  2. ready-for-pickup — otherwise, Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold.
  3. waiting — otherwise.

When a hold leaves the view. A hold is listed from Hold Placed until it ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, when the holder checks the tool out, when the tool is retired or recorded lost, or when the holder closes their account. In events:

  • Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for the hold;
  • Tool Checked Out for the hold's tool by the hold's neighbor;
  • Tool Retired or Tool Lost for the hold's tool;
  • Neighbor Account Closed for the holder.

Queue order. A tool's queue is the order in which Hold Placed was recorded for it. To work out positions, the view keeps, for each tool, every hold on it that hasn't ended, with its holder and whether it has been fulfilled. This is bookkeeping, not part of the row, and other neighbors' holds are never returned.

Queries

  • List my holds. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns every hold of that neighbor that hasn't ended, each with every field above, and nothing about anyone else's holds (INV-MYHD-1). There is no paging. A neighbor with no holds gets an empty list. Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when the hold was placed, in the order Hold Placed was recorded (INV-MYHD-18).

Invariants / Business Rules

A neighbor has at most one hold on any one tool, because Place Hold refuses a second (INV-HOLD-7, Place Hold). A suspended neighbor can't place a new hold (INV-HOLD-9) or collect a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-7), but may still cancel. An expired hold sends no message, doesn't count against the neighbor, and the neighbor may place a new hold on the tool at the back of the queue (Expire Hold). A suspended neighbor keeps their holds and their place in each queue. A front holder who can't collect, because they are suspended or have an overdue loan, still has the tool set aside for them, and the pickup window runs regardless (Fulfill Hold, INV-FUL-8). These rules are owned by those slices; this view just reflects the events they record, and it doesn't hear suspension or loans at all (INV-MYHD-11).

  • INV-MYHD-1: A neighbor's My Holds shows only their own holds.
    • The query returns only holds whose holder is the neighbor ID it is given. It never shows who else holds a tool, only the neighbor's own position. No neighbor-facing screen ever shows who has a tool or who holds one; only the shed manager sees borrowers, on Tool Inventory.
  • INV-MYHD-2: Holds on a tool queue in the order they were placed. Each waiting hold shows the neighbor's position in that tool's queue.
    • Position 1 is the next hold to be fulfilled. A hold moves up as holds ahead of it are fulfilled or end.
    • A hold that has been fulfilled is no longer in the waiting queue, so the first waiting hold behind a set-aside is at position 1.
  • INV-MYHD-3: Once a neighbor's hold is fulfilled, My Holds shows the tool as ready for pickup, with the date to collect it by.
    • The collect-by date is the one Hold Fulfilled carries: the date the tool was set aside plus 3 days. My Holds shows it as recorded and never works it out itself.
    • My Holds is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is set aside for them. The Tool Catalog is the same for every neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-4: A hold that is ready for pickup stays on My Holds until the holder collects it, cancels it, or Hold Expired is recorded for it. Then it drops off.
    • The tool then passes to the next hold, which shows as ready for pickup on that neighbor's My Holds once Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • INV-MYHD-5: When a holder checks out the tool they hold, their hold ends and drops off My Holds, whether or not it had been fulfilled.
    • The loan then appears on My Loans.
  • INV-MYHD-6: A cancelled hold drops off My Holds, whether it was waiting or ready for pickup.
    • Cancelling a hold that is ready for pickup passes the tool to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-7: Retiring a tool, or recording it lost, ends every hold on it, and those holds drop off My Holds.
    • The holders are not told.
  • INV-MYHD-8: Closing an account ends all of that neighbor's holds. Their holds drop off My Holds, and holds behind them move up.
    • A tool that was ready for pickup for them passes to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-13: Once a tool is set aside for a neighbor, My Holds shows whether the pickup email was sent or couldn't be delivered.
    • If the email can't be delivered, the tool stays ready for pickup, with the same collect-by date.
  • INV-MYHD-14: Each hold shows the tool's name.
    • The name comes with Hold Placed, which carries it.
  • INV-MYHD-11: Only Hold Placed, Hold Cancelled, Hold Fulfilled, Pickup Notice Sent, Pickup Notice Failed, Hold Expired, Tool Checked Out by a holder of that tool, Tool Retired, Tool Lost and Neighbor Account Closed change My Holds.
    • A checkout by anyone else leaves every neighbor's My Holds unchanged.
  • INV-MYHD-15: Applying the same event twice leaves My Holds as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYHD-16: My Holds offers Cancel on every hold it lists.
    • That includes holds ready for pickup, holds whose pickup window has ended, and holds of a suspended neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-17: Once a set-aside's collect-by date has passed, My Holds shows that the pickup window has ended, even before Hold Expired is recorded.
    • From the start of the day after the collect-by date, in the shed's local time, the set-aside is no longer theirs: the tool goes to the next neighbor in the queue, or to whoever checks it out first if nobody is waiting (INV-CHK-3b, Check Out Tool). The hold drops off when Hold Expired is recorded.
  • INV-MYHD-18: Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when they were placed.
  • INV-MYHD-19: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYHD-20: My Holds is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Hold placed (INV-MYHD-2, INV-MYHD-14, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ana has T1, the "Cordless drill", on loan, and nobody has a hold on it
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on T1, carrying the name "Cordless drill"
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H1: "Cordless drill", waiting, position 1, pickup notice none, with Cancel offered.
  • A second hold placed (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Cara's My Holds lists H2, waiting, position 2. Ben's is unchanged.
  • Holds placed in the same instant (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's H2 and then Dan's H3 on T1, with the same placedAt
    • Then: H2 is at position 2 and H3 at position 3: the order recorded decides, not placedAt.
  • Hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has been returned
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, with the collect-by date 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, with no position. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Pickup email sent (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, pickup notice none
    • When: Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice sent.
  • Pickup email couldn't be delivered (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, pickup notice sent
    • When: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice undelivered, still ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Collect-by date is the last day (INV-MYHD-17)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October
    • When: his holds are listed at 23:59 on 17 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 is ready-for-pickup.
  • Pickup window ended, not yet expired (INV-MYHD-17, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded
    • When: his holds are listed at 00:00 on 18 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 shows pickup-window-ended, with Cancel still offered.
  • Hold expired (INV-MYHD-4)
    • Given: Ben's H1 shows pickup-window-ended, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting at position 1 until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Suspended holder (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-11)
    • Given: Ben is suspended, and his H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: T1 is returned and Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, collect by 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Holder collects the tool (INV-MYHD-5)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Ben
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's is unchanged.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-MYHD-5, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has just been returned
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Ben, before Hold Fulfilled
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Ready-for-pickup hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Tool retired (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for T1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan as loan L1, and Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L1, the loan of T1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-MYHD-8)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ben
    • Then: H1 drops off. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold again after expiry (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 expired, and T1 is now set aside for Cara's H2
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's new hold H4 on T1
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H4, waiting, position 1, behind Cara's set-aside.
  • Checkout by a neighbor with no hold (INV-MYHD-11)
    • Given: Ana has no holds, and the hammer (T5) is available
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T5 and Ana
    • Then: no neighbor's My Holds changes.
  • Only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1)
    • Given: Ben has H1 and Cara has H2, both on T1
    • When: Ben's holds are listed
    • Then: only H1 is returned, with its position. Nothing about H2 or Cara is returned.
  • List order (INV-MYHD-18)
    • Given: Ben placed H5 on the ladder, then H1 on the cordless drill
    • When: his holds are listed
    • Then: H1 (cordless drill) comes first, then H5 (ladder).
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYHD-15)
    • Given: Ben's My Holds lists H1 at position 1
    • When: the same Hold Placed for H1 is applied again
    • Then: Ben's My Holds still lists H1 once, at position 1, and no later hold's position changes.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYHD-19)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Holds is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYHD-20)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: the holds of N1, Ana, are asked for
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own holds." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-MYHD-19
requester-mismatch You can only see your own holds. INV-MYHD-20
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYHD-15). An event applied a second time leaves the view as it was after the first.
  • Events for a hold that has ended: once a hold has ended it is gone from this view. A later event for it (a replay, or a Pickup Notice Failed that arrives after the set-aside ended) changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: Cancel offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, just as the hold expires or the tool is collected). Cancel Hold checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may list only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  • PII & compliance: shows a neighbor their own holds only, and never who else holds or has a tool. The other holders and borrowers it keeps for working out positions are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, placedAt.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Pickup Notice Sent (Send Pickup Notice): holdId.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (Record Pickup Notice Failure): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId. This view matches it by toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Hold Placed and Tool Checked Out match slices/place-hold.md and slices/check-out-tool.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Cancel Hold.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":25,"name":"Undelivered Notices — pickup notice failed","x0":4361.76,"x1":4505.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Undelivered Notices

Intent

Shows the shed manager every email the shed couldn't deliver — overdue notices and pickup notices — so they can reach the neighbor another way. A neighbor who wasn't told their loan is overdue, or that a tool is waiting for them, doesn't stay unnoticed. An entry stays only while there is something to follow up.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Undelivered Notices screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per failed overdue notice whose loan is still open, and one per failed pickup notice whose set-aside hasn't ended, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. The screen offers no actions. Following up is the shed manager's job, in person; no email is tried again after its failure is recorded (Send Overdue Notice, INV-OVN-9).
  • Which failure reports become events is decided by the two failure slices: a report that matches no notice the shed sent, or that arrives after the loan or set-aside has ended, is ignored there and never reaches this view.

Read Model / View

  • View: Undelivered Notices built from events: "Overdue Notice Failed", "Pickup Notice Failed", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Tool Returned", "Tool Lost", "Hold Fulfilled", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Expired", "Tool Retired", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the Undelivered Notices screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. An entry appears, changes or drops off shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes).

One row per entry. LoanId, HoldId, ToolId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be empty.

Field Type Source / Notes
kind Text overdue-notice or pickup-notice. Derived: from which failure event created the entry.
loanId LoanId Optional; overdue-notice entries only. Overdue Notice Failed.loanId.
holdId HoldId Optional; pickup-notice entries only. Derived: Pickup Notice Failed.holdId.
neighborId NeighborId The borrower (Tool Checked Out.neighborId for the loan) or the holder (Hold Fulfilled.neighborId for the hold).
neighborName Text Derived: Tool Checked Out.neighborName for an overdue notice, Hold Fulfilled.neighborName for a pickup notice.
neighborEmail Text Derived: Tool Checked Out.neighborEmail or Hold Fulfilled.neighborEmail, replaced by each later Neighbor Email Changed.email. Always the current one.
toolId ToolId Tool Checked Out.toolId for the loan, or Hold Fulfilled.toolId for the hold.
toolName Text Derived: Tool Checked Out.toolName for an overdue notice, Hold Fulfilled.toolName for a pickup notice.
dueDate Date Optional; overdue-notice entries only. Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for the loan.
collectByDate Date Optional; pickup-notice entries only. Derived: Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate for the hold.
reason Text refused or bounced, from the failure event's reason.
failedAt Instant From the failure event's failedAt. Shown as the failure date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

To fill an entry the moment its failure lands, the view also keeps, for every open loan, its tool, borrower and current due date, and for every live set-aside, its tool, holder and collect-by date. These are bookkeeping, not rows, and are never returned.

When an entry drops off.

  • An overdue-notice entry drops off when its loan ends: Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan. Retiring the tool while it is out doesn't end the loan, so the entry stays.
  • A pickup-notice entry drops off when its set-aside ends: the holder checks the tool out (Tool Checked Out for that tool and holder), or Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for the hold, or Tool Retired for the tool, or Neighbor Account Closed for the holder.

Nothing brings an entry back.

Queries

  • List undelivered notices. Takes nothing. Returns every entry with all the fields above. There is no paging. Entries are listed by neighbor name, then by failedAt, the time the entry was created (INV-UDN-9).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-UDN-1: Every Overdue Notice Failed and every Pickup Notice Failed creates exactly one entry.
    • Nothing else creates an entry. A failure is recorded only after the email provider has made its 3 delivery attempts over about an hour and reported a final failure, so the shed manager never sees a notice that is still being tried.
  • INV-UDN-2: Each entry shows the failure date, and whether the provider refused the email or it bounced.
    • A bounce usually means a wrong email address. The shed manager can ask the neighbor to change it from My Account.
  • INV-UDN-3: An overdue-notice entry shows the borrower's name and current email, the tool's name, and the loan's current due date.
    • The name, the email, the tool's name and the due date come from Tool Checked Out, the email as replaced by any later Neighbor Email Changed and the due date as moved by any Loan Extended.
  • INV-UDN-3a: A pickup-notice entry shows the holder's name and current email, the tool's name, and the collect-by date.
    • The collect-by date is the one recorded on Hold Fulfilled. Name, email and tool name come from the same events as for an overdue-notice entry.
  • INV-UDN-4: An overdue-notice entry drops off when its loan ends: the tool is returned, or the shed manager records it lost.
    • Either way the loan has ended, and there is nothing left to follow up. A tool retired while out keeps its entry until one of these happens.
  • INV-UDN-5: A pickup-notice entry drops off when its set-aside ends.
    • A set-aside ends when the holder collects the tool, or the hold is cancelled or expires, or it ends because the tool was retired or the holder closed their account.
  • INV-UDN-9: Entries are listed by neighbor name, ignoring case, then by when the failure was recorded.
    • The same order as every list in the shed.
  • INV-UDN-8: Applying the same event twice leaves Undelivered Notices as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-UDN-10: Only the shed manager can read Undelivered Notices.
    • A signed-in caller without the shed-manager role is refused with not-shed-manager, and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in. Nothing is returned to either.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana Ruiz registered with ana@example.org and has the cordless drill on loan L1, due 12 October. Ben Ito registered with ben@example.org, and Hold Fulfilled was recorded for his hold H1 on the hedge trimmer with a collect-by date of 16 October.

  • Overdue notice fails (INV-UDN-1, INV-UDN-2, INV-UDN-3)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices is empty
    • When: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1 on 13 October, as bounced
    • Then: Undelivered Notices lists an overdue-notice entry: Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, the cordless drill, due 12 October, failed 13 October, bounced.
  • Due date shown after an extension (INV-UDN-3)
    • Given: Loan Extended moved L1's due date to 19 October, and the loan is now overdue
    • When: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1 on 20 October, as refused
    • Then: the entry shows the due date 19 October, failed 20 October, refused.
  • Pickup notice fails (INV-UDN-1, INV-UDN-2, INV-UDN-3a)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry
    • When: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1 on 13 October, as refused
    • Then: Undelivered Notices also lists a pickup-notice entry: Ben Ito, ben@example.org, the hedge trimmer, collect by 16 October, failed 13 October, refused. Ana's entry is unchanged.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-UDN-8)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry once
    • When: the same Overdue Notice Failed for L1 is applied again
    • Then: the entry is still listed once.
  • Tool returned (INV-UDN-4)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry for L1
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1
    • Then: Ana's entry drops off.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-UDN-4)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry for L1
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L1
    • Then: Ana's entry drops off.
  • Tool retired while out (INV-UDN-4)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry for L1
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the cordless drill
    • Then: Ana's entry stays. It drops off once L1 is returned or recorded lost.
  • Holder collects the tool (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the hedge trimmer and Ben
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Someone else checks out the tool (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1, and his collect-by date has passed, but Hold Expired hasn't been recorded
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the hedge trimmer and Cara
    • Then: Ben's entry stays until Hold Expired is recorded for H1, and then drops off.
  • Holder cancels the hold (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Set-aside expires (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Tool retired while set aside (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the hedge trimmer
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ben
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Neighbor corrects their email (INV-UDN-3)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry, showing ana@example.org, the address that bounced
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: Ana's entry shows ana.ruiz@example.net. The entry stays until L1 is returned or recorded lost.
  • Listing order (INV-UDN-9)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry (failed 13 October), Ana's overdue-notice entry (failed 14 October) and Ana's pickup-notice entry (failed 12 October)
    • When: the shed manager lists undelivered notices
    • Then: the entries come back as: Ana's pickup-notice entry, Ana's overdue-notice entry, then Ben's.
  • Listing undelivered notices
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry and Ben's pickup-notice entry
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists undelivered notices
    • Then: both entries are returned with all their fields, with no paging.
  • A neighbor tries to read the list (INV-UDN-10)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices has entries
    • When: a neighbor, signed in without the shed-manager role, asks for the undelivered notices
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can see this screen." Nothing is returned.
  • No sign-in (INV-UDN-10)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices has entries
    • When: a caller with no sign-in asks for the undelivered notices
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Read refusals: the list query refuses a caller without the shed-manager role with not-shed-manager ("Only the shed manager can see this screen."), and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in ("Please sign in."). Nothing is returned on a refusal. These mean the same conditions as in the shed manager's commands.
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-UDN-8). An event applied a second time leaves the entries as they were after the first.
  • Ended loans and set-asides: a failure report for a loan or set-aside that has already ended is ignored by Record Overdue Notice Failure and Record Pickup Notice Failure, so no entry is ever created for one. An entry, once it drops off, never comes back.
  • No actions: the screen issues no commands. Its only use is to prompt the shed manager to follow up in person.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Undelivered Notices screen is the shed manager's alone; neighbors never see it. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role; only a caller with it may read this view.
  • PII & compliance: shows neighbors' names, current emails and the tools they have or are waiting for, to the shed manager only. An entry is kept only while its loan or set-aside is live. Names and emails themselves are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Overdue Notice Failed (Record Overdue Notice Failure): loanId, reason, failedAt.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (Record Pickup Notice Failure): holdId, reason, failedAt.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, toolName, neighborId, neighborName, neighborEmail, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool), Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, collectByDate.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs. Hold Fulfilled carrying toolId and neighborId is this view's assumption, because it doesn't hear Hold Placed; Fulfill Hold is checked against it when it is written in depth.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen issues no commands.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":26,"name":"Pickups To Expire","x0":4530.76,"x1":4674.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Pickups To Expire

Intent

The pickup expirer's to-do list: every tool currently set aside for a holder, with the date it must be collected by. The expirer works through the ones whose collect-by date has passed, so a set-aside the holder doesn't collect in time ends and the tool moves on to the next neighbor.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Pickup Expirer, a system processor in the Expire Hold slice (slices/expire-hold.md). No person or screen reads this list.
  • What the expirer does with it: it reads the set-asides that are due to expire, and issues Expire Hold for each.

Read Model / View

  • View: Pickups To Expire built from events: "Hold Fulfilled", "Tool Checked Out", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Expired", "Tool Retired", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the Pickup Expirer (Expire Hold). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a set-aside joins or leaves shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a set-aside is due to expire is worked out when the list is read, from collectByDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it becomes due from the first read after the midnight that ends its collect-by date.

The view keeps one row for every live set-aside; the query returns only those due to expire. HoldId, ToolId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

Field Type Source / Notes
holdId HoldId Hold Fulfilled.holdId.
toolId ToolId Hold Fulfilled.toolId.
neighborId NeighborId Hold Fulfilled.neighborId: the holder.
collectByDate Date Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate, as recorded there. Never worked out here.
dueToExpire Bool Derived: yes when today's date in the shed's local time zone is after collectByDate (INV-PTE-2). Worked out when the list is read.

When a row leaves the view. A set-aside's row is removed when:

  • Tool Checked Out is recorded for its tool by its holder (matching toolId and neighborId);
